To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a large number (approximately 18%) of genes were up- or down-regulated during the 6-8-weeks of placental villi development, and that these genes were involved in biological processes including regulation of cell growth, proliferation and apoptosis, angiogenesis, and immune and inflammatory responses.

the expression profile of genes in the first trimesters of placenta development are highly dynamic and the genes involved in ion homeostasis and metabolism are highly up-regulated during the last week of first trimester placenta development.
the transcript expression profiles of human first trimester placentas during 6-, 8-weeks are distinct and the expression profiles are more similar to 6-weeks than 8-weeks in 7-weeks placenta.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comprehensive analysis of transcript expression profile in human placental first trimester samples using a custom-tailor-made cDNA array.
the identification of genes that are differentially expressed during 6- to 8-weeks human placental villus development.

the identification and characterization of genes and gene products that are differentially regulated between 6, 7, 8 weeks of placental villi and the identification of the molecular mechanisms that are responsible for these differences in the developing placental villi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transcriptome of human placental first trimester villi during 4-8 weeks of pregnancy is highly dynamic and the present study provides a unique insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying the early placental development.

the expression profile of genes in first trimester human placental villus is dynamic and complex and that this dynamic expression pattern is a consequence of the rapid growth and development of placental villi in the first trimesters.
the transcript expression profile of human first trimester villi is highly dynamic, complex and specific, and that this profile is highly dependent on chronological age of placenta.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our data suggest that a network of genes involved in cell proliferation, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix and immune responses are highly regulated during the early stage of placental development.

the expression profiles of 400 genes in first trimester placenta during 6- to 8-weeks are highly dynamic and these genes are involved mainly in regulation of cell growth, proliferation, anti-apotosis, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix remodeling.

the present study has provided an initial molecular characterization of the human placental villus during the first trimester of pregnancy and the findings would be helpful for understanding the developmental characteristics and molecular mechanisms of the human placenta during early pregnancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptome of human placental tissue during first trimester of pregnancy is highly dynamic and is characterized by a complex network of gene interactions.
the expression of a number of genes is differentially regulated during the 6-8-weeks of placental villi growth.
